Appearance:

Ms. Shikha Baghel - Panel Lawyer for State.

Order 
This is the first Criminal Appeal filed by the appellant under Section 14-A (1) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (POA) Act, 1989 seeking bail in connection with Crime No.385 of 2024 registered at Police Station - Bhalumada, District - Anuppur, for offences punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 294, 506 of IPC and Section 3(2)(v) and 3(1)(w)(ii) of SC & ST (POA) Act.

sentences.text:
2. Learned counsel for appellant has submitted that there was a consensual relationship between the two adult person and the dispute took place regarding money transaction that was Rs.12 lakh and no case of the rape is made out as the victim was knowing the consequences, hence, the appellant be released on bail.
3. Learned counsel for objector has submitted that the victim's father was employee in SCCL and after retirement he got the money and distributed among his children and more than Rs.12 lakh was received by the victim and when this fact came to the knowledge of appellant, he approached and gave the assurance that he will marry with the victim and on that pretext, made sexual relations and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12228 2 CRA-2288-2025 extorted the money and when victim asked for marriage, he abruptly denied and also did not give the money, therefore, FIR was lodged against the appellant, hence, appellant is not entitled for bail.

4. Learned counsel for State has opposed the bail application and has submitted that the victim has supported her version recorded under Section 183 of the BNSS, 2023 and from the bank record money transaction is proved, hence, appellant is not entitled for bail.

sentences.text: Heard the parties and perused the record.

6. Looking to the period of relation and the fact that victim was more than 30 year and trial will take time to conclude, but without commenting anything on merits of the case, bail application filed on behalf of appellant is allowed.
7.

It is directed that appellant shall be enlarged on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, and the appellant shall be remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates as may be fixed by trial Court for his regular appearance.
8. He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
C.C. as per rules.
